updates.statement: Accuracy noise sets the usable margin, and decisions near the gate select for luck. Single-component model (E113): any fp-level difference, whether a math-neutral recipe change or a new cuDNN pick set in a fresh process, fully decorrelates a seed's trajectory. Per-trajectory sd is ~0.26 pp, and seeds carry no persistent component (paired-difference sd 0.36 pp = sqrt(2) x 0.26). Expected sds: 3-seed scored mean ~0.15 pp; 22-seed mean ~0.055 pp; 100-seed mean ~0.026 pp. Two-arm SE = 0.26*sqrt(1/nA + 1/nB), where n counts distinct (non-bit-identical) trajectories. E101's 0.45 pp gap (~2 SD of a difference) and E106's 0.03 pp process sd (n=3, 90% CI ~0.25x-2.2x) are both consistent with this. Consequences: (1) most 8-22-seed off-seed deltas (E078, E079, E084, E092, E104, E105, E107, E110-E112) are <=~1.4 SE, and only E093 (-0.44) and E083 (-0.29) are clearly real; (2) gate passes are population margin plus luck (E100 pop. ~0.7530, local pass p ~50%); (3) the official 40-seed mean has sd ~0.04 pp, so a pop. mean >=0.7515 clears 0.75 almost surely.

updates.statement: Run-to-run noise on the 3-seed scored mean (~0.15 pp sd, from 0.26/sqrt(3)) is the decision-relevant noise for the gate, and picking whichever near-threshold variant first clears 0.753 selects for luck (E026, E046, E068, E090, E096, E100). Comparisons must count distinct trajectories, not runs: two bit-identical scored runs are one sample.
updates.reason: Numbers restated under the single-component model (E113); a separate per-process component is no longer assumed.
Superseded. Its free step (cross-process sd) is answered by E113's one-component model, (2) is met, and (3) (E095 vs E090) is a ~1-SE question that no longer drives the tip lineage.

E113: fp-level perturbations fully decorrelate trajectories, so cuDNN pick sets are just more independent draws. The E098/E101 vs E106 'disagreement' is sampling noise in an sd estimated from n=3 processes. Nothing left for a per-process offset to explain.
Parent retired. At most a free log analysis; no runs.

updates.statement: Effective sample size is the number of distinct (non-bit-identical) trajectories, whether they come from new seeds or new fresh processes on the same seeds. Seed pairing gives no variance reduction (E113: paired sd 0.36 = sqrt(2) x 0.26), so large-seed A/Bs are two-sample comparisons with SE = 0.26*sqrt(1/nA + 1/nB). 100 vs 100 gives SE ~0.037 pp. A pooled >=200-trajectory baseline gives ~0.032 against a 100-trajectory arm. Untimed trials (~4.5 s) make ~100 trajectories per ~8 min.
updates.reason: E113 contradicts the earlier claim that only more seeds, not more processes, help; corrected per review.
E113: paired-difference sd 0.36 pp, SE 0.036, difference -0.056 (within 2 SE). Prediction met. The 'pairing helps' branch is refuted (sd > 0.15), so later A/Bs are unpaired.
The premise (side-script sd too small vs scored) is explained by n=3 sd-estimation noise under the E113 model. No evidence that the instruments differ.
Parent retired.

E113 (same seed under a neutral perturbation is uncorrelated with itself) and search 2304.01910 (independent per-run errors) rule out a persistent recipe x seed offset on seeds 0-2. E100's five distinct scored samples (mean 0.7543, SE ~0.067) are within ~0.2 SE of its 100-seed mean (~0.7530): luck plus margin.
Answered without a run by E113; not worth compute.

updates.statement: Per-epoch GPU work drives the score. Falsifiable core: in the energy-bound 32 px phase (~71% of time), wall time tracks activation bytes moved in backward more than FLOPs. So cutting backward through the high-resolution early layers (stem + group 1 at 31x31) saves more than their FLOP share, while width cuts in the low-resolution group 2 save less than theirs (E080: 33-60% recovered). E116 is the first supporting point: freezing stem + group 1 over the last 15% of samples saved 3.6-4.5% of total time, implying a ~15-20% cheaper 32 px step vs a ~13% backward FLOP share. Tip E100 is ~4.46 s (pop. mean ~0.7530). Closed time levers: CUDA graphs, Inductor tuning, cuDNN determinism, benchmark_limit, prepare, group-2 width, whitening-bias freeze, 32 px trims at a poorly measured rate, and the 28 px substitution. Live: the late-freeze dose-response (H2.20), group-1 width (N_g1w), depth cuts (H2.18, low), group-3 width (H2.19, low).
updates.reason: Review: the old Lvl1 was near-tautological. E116 is the live result and points to a byte mechanism that no node predicted.

updates.statement: Late layer freezing is a real time lever with a small, real accuracy cost. Detaching group 1's output (no backward into group 1 or the stem) from 85% of samples saved 3.6% scored (4.5% dev) at -0.12 pp vs E113 arm A, or ~-0.09 pp vs the pooled 200-trajectory E100 baseline (~3 SE). That is ~0.025-0.033 pp per 1%, as good as or better than any measured trade. External priors are consistent: MosaicML ~5% throughput with no Pareto gain, FreezeOut null on VGG-like nets. So it is a rate lever, not free. Open: the shape of the dose-response, whether a stochastic/progressive freeze trades better, and whether the loss fits within the accepted population margin.
updates.reason: E116 confirmed the time saving (step-1 profile cleared the >=8% gate; trials without recompiles) and a ~3 SE accuracy loss. Search (Drop-Muon, MosaicML, FreezeOut) frames it as a rate lever.

E116: time saving met (-3.6% scored, prediction >=3%). Accuracy -0.12 vs arm A / ~-0.09 vs the pooled baseline straddles the <=0.1 pp bar. The scored-vs-dev ~1% time gap is unexplained. Decided by the dose-response node.

updates.statement: Per-phase batch size. Large early batches hurt (E043, -0.49 pp, 3 seeds, warmup-confounded). Smaller batches may buy accuracy: bs 1024 at 32 px gave +0.11 off-seed (E084, 8 seeds), and bs 1024 everywhere +0.12 (E104, 8 seeds). Each is ~0.9 SE under the corrected model (SE ~0.13 pp), so neither the gain nor a rate of ~0.04-0.065 pp per 1% is established. The tip's bs-1024 late phases are kept as inherited, not as a proven gain.
updates.reason: Review: the 8-seed deltas were judged with SEs that assumed pairing helps; under E113 they are ~1 SE.
E084/E085 scored +0.18 (two runs, SE ~0.15) and off-seed +0.11 on 8 seeds (SE ~0.13): ~1 SE each. Not established.
E095 vs E084 off-seed equality is two 8-seed means (SE ~0.13); it cannot separate update count from window length.

updates.statement: On the Muon tip, adding optimizer updates (smaller batches) at fixed epochs might raise accuracy at ~0.04-0.065 pp per 1% of time. The evidence (E084 +0.11, E104 +0.12, 8 seeds each) is ~1 SE apiece, so the rate is unmeasured. Larger phase-local Muon lr gave no gain >=0.1 (E107, E110, E111, E100 vs E090). Only relevant as a way to fund a real loss such as E116's, and only after a 100-seed measurement (N_e104).
updates.reason: Review: neither the update-count rate nor its mechanism is distinguishable from zero at current resolution.
Placement question: E114 (+0.02 vs arm A, ~+0.045 vs pooled, SE ~0.033) says any placement effect is small. The rival (H11.2) is retired. The H10.1/H11 comparison is no longer decision-relevant.
Status unchanged (inconclusive). Note: the token E104- is relative to the early-fragility rival, not to this statement. Relative to this prediction E104 is ~ (inside the band, ~1 SE).

updates.statement: (Restated as a lever) A larger phase-local Muon lr buys >=0.1 pp at zero time. Tests: low-res x1.5 (E107) -0.02, 28 px x1.25 (E111) +0.03, 32 px x1.5 vs x1.25 (E110) -0.07, pooled E100 (32 px x1.25) vs E090 +0.01 (22-66 trajectories each, SE ~0.05-0.08). Effects >=~0.15 pp are excluded; the mechanistic contrast with update count is not established because the update-count gain itself is ~1 SE.
updates.reason: Review: the mechanism claim compared ~1-SE effects. Keep only the lever-level conclusion, which four arms support.

E114, the pre-registered decisive test (100 seeds), gave +0.02 vs arm A (~+0.045 vs pooled, SE ~0.033) for shifting 32 px time into 24 px. Neither H11 nor its rival shows a material effect, and the node's own text leaned against it.
Parent retired; E114 null on placement.
Parent retired.

updates.statement: The schedule sits near a flat optimum along the low-res/high-res reallocation axis, with concave returns. Large removals of early quality cost a lot (no 24 px bridge -0.68 pp, E032; whitening bias frozen at ~3% -0.44 pp, E093, ~3.5 SE). Small equal-time reallocations are null (E114: ~+0.02-0.045 pp, SE ~0.033, for +0.5 ep at 24 px vs -0.25 ep at 32 px). No further 16/24 px removal or reallocation runs are warranted.
updates.reason: Review: 'asymmetry' is just concave returns, and E114 nulled reallocation.
E114: +0.02 vs arm A, ~+0.045 vs the pooled 200-trajectory baseline (SE ~0.033), at +0.3-0.5% time. Even if real, converting it into time via a trim nets <0.5%. Not worth more runs.
Still inconclusive. Superseded by E114's 100-seed measurement.
E114: +0.02 (vs arm A) to ~+0.045 (vs pooled baseline), below the >=+0.08 support bar and above the <=-0.05 refute bar. The reallocation axis is closed as low-value.

updates.statement: (Narrowed) Under Muon, the averaging design (lookahead-EMA ramp shape/cadence, final-EMA lerp) is the main remaining zero-time accuracy source not yet tuned. These pieces were inherited from SGD/Fable and never tuned under Muon, but the premise is weak: the ablations that suggested they carry ~0.2 pp (E092 lookahead -0.18, E079 final EMA -0.18) are 8-seed deltas of ~1.4 SE. Only window length was varied (E081, E083 worse; E083 ~2.3 SE). The old structural-vs-scalar split is dropped: it was drawn after the results came in, and large moves on 'scalar' knobs (E027, E031, E093) also hurt.
updates.reason: Review: the structural/scalar split cannot be falsified. Narrowed to the one concrete claim it supported, with lowered confidence.

updates.statement: Averaging strength under Muon. Lookahead (every 3 steps at bs 1536, airbench-style ramp) and the final 8-step EMA (lerp 0.3) were never tuned under Muon. hiverge's CIFAR-10 Muon SOTA uses no training-time averaging, while airbench's lookahead uses decay 0.95^5*(t/T)^3, i.e. almost no early smoothing. Premise to verify first: removing lookahead costs >=0.1 pp on >=100 trajectories (E092 was -0.18 on 8 seeds, ~1.4 SE). If it does not, averaging strength is not a lever.
updates.reason: Review: the premise (E092, E079) rests on ~1.4-SE ablations. Search: hiverge has no averaging, and airbench's cubic ramp gives concrete shape arms. Confidence lowered.

updates.statement: Gated on a 100-seed lookahead-removal re-measure showing >=0.1 pp loss vs the pooled E100 baseline. Then, on E100 (host-side scalars or 0-d tensors only, nothing recompiles), run arms judged on >=100 trajectories each vs the pooled baseline: lookahead ramp exponent 2 and 4 (vs the current cubic), peak decay x0.8 and x1.2, and final-EMA lerp 0.2 and 0.4 (window fixed at the last 8 steps). Prediction: at least one arm gains >=+0.08 pp (~2.5 SE vs pooled). If every arm is within +/-0.05 pp, averaging strength is closed (effects >=~0.1 pp excluded).
updates.reason: Search (airbench cubic ramp) gives better-motivated arms. Review: the premise rests on ~1.4-SE ablations and must be re-measured first.
H12.2 refuted by E112 (~66 trajectories). The remaining children (multiplicity, translate strength) have weak external priors (search: gains only at long budgets or with added compute).
E112: 3 processes x 22 seeds, mean -0.03 pp (SE ~0.045), ~2.9 SE below the predicted +0.1. Class-balanced batches are not a lever here.
E112: -0.03 pp vs a +0.1 prediction (~2.9 SE). The node was left 'open' despite the E112- token; corrected.

updates.statement: Muon momentum and lr sit near a local optimum. Momentum is flat in 0.5-0.6 and steep above (E027 -1.18 pp at 0.85). For lr, effects >=~0.15 pp are excluded from 0.20 to ~0.36 effective across all phases (E034, E105, E107, E110, E111, each within +/-0.09 pp on 8-66 trajectories). That does not show the lr is flat to +/-0.05. Muon lr scaling is closed as a lever at the current instrument's resolution.
updates.reason: Review: '+/-0.05 closes it' claims exceed the instrument's resolution; restated as an exclusion bound.
Search 2602.06797: CIFAR-100 (vs an easy binary task) preferred a stable phase with decay over the last 40%. Slight prior raise. The regime (12.5k tiny-batch SGD steps) is far from ~280 Muon steps.

updates.statement: Step-indexed schedule reshuffles and trims are no longer a usable lever at the current margin. Low-res reshuffles are exhausted (E070/E071 vs E072/E073; E114 null on reallocation). The 32 px trim rate (~0.065 pp per 1%, E088/E089 vs E084/E085) comes from two scored runs per arm and is uncertain by about +/-50%. It needs a 100-seed re-measure before it serves as the yardstick for other levers (N_trim).
updates.reason: Review: the yardstick rate is itself ~+/-0.15 pp. Note: the E047+ token reflects an earlier, opposite reading of this node.

updates.statement: The judge is a 300 W A100 PCIe; local runs are on a 400 W SXM4. Untimed analysis of existing NVML logs (E045, E116 step-1 profile, E100), with no power-limit changes: project each candidate's judge time as the sum over phases of max(phase energy / 300 W, phase GPU-busy time). Prediction: E116's freeze saving is a larger fraction on the projected judge than locally (>=1.1x), because it removes energy-bound backward bytes, while bs-1024 per-step levers transfer worse. Use only to break ties between configs whose local times are within 3%.
updates.reason: Review: freeze and width cuts are byte levers, so the free judge-transfer projection is now decision-relevant for E116.

Status stays refuted. Token signs are inverted relative to the negated statement ('Muon does not help'): E019/E020/E024 refute it, so they should read '-'. Interpret existing '+' tokens as refuting evidence.

Status unchanged. E032-/E041- tokens refer to the 'more 16/20 px swaps are free' reading; relative to the statement as written (each swap costs 0.2-0.35 pp, no further swap affordable) they are supporting. Interpret accordingly.

new.statement: In the energy-bound 32 px phase, the backward of the high-resolution early layers (stem + group 1 on 31x31x128 activations: conv wgrad/dgrad, BN/GELU backward) costs >=1.3x its FLOP share of the step. Its BN/GELU backward passes over the largest activations dominate memory traffic and energy, which the fused elementwise kernels' ~30% GPU-time share (E067) and E116's ~15-20% step saving (vs ~13% backward-FLOP share) both suggest. Consequence: byte cuts at high resolution (late freeze, group-1 width, early downsampling) trade better than FLOP-equivalent cuts in group 2/3.

Untimed profile on E100 at 32 px / bs 1024 (static graphs, warmed in build): per-group backward GPU time and NVML energy, plus bytes read/written by the BN/GELU backward kernels per group. Prediction: stem + group 1 account for >=1.3x their backward-FLOP share of backward energy (>=17% vs ~13%), and the detached-variant step from E116's step-1 profile is >=15% cheaper per step. If the ratio is <1.1x, E116's saving needs another explanation (e.g. removed optimizer work for group-1 params), and N_bytes is refuted.

Group-1 width as a byte lever, never tested under Muon (H2.6 dismissed it on an SGD-era FLOP estimate). Free first: read the logged kernel tile shapes for group-1 convs. Then an untimed profile on E100 of group-1 widths 96 (1.5x64) and 112 vs 128, at 32/28 px bs 1024 and 24/16 px bs 1536 (all shapes warmed). Width 96 cuts ~13% of conv FLOPs (g1 convs plus g2 conv1 input) and 25% of the 31x31 activation bytes. Prediction: width 96 saves >=5% of projected total time, i.e. it recovers >=70% of its FLOP-proportional saving, unlike group 2's 33-60% (E080). Score only if >=5%, and judge accuracy on >=100 trajectories vs the pooled E100 baseline, requiring <=0.03 pp loss per 1% saved. Low prior: capacity is valuable on CIFAR-100 (E017, E050).

Dose-response of the late group-1 + stem freeze on E100 (both graph variants and every renorm x freeze flag combination warmed in build, checked with TORCH_LOGS=recompiles on a 2-trial dev run). Freeze points: 92%, 85% (E116) and 75% of samples (75% lies in the 32 px phase, which starts at ~60%). Predictions: (a) time saving scales roughly with frozen 32 px samples, ~2%, ~4% and ~6.5%; (b) accuracy loss vs the pooled 200-trajectory E100 baseline, on >=100 trajectories each, stays <=0.03 pp per 1% at 85-92% and is steeper (>0.04 pp per 1%) at 75%, because early layers still adapt (E093). Also explain E116's scored-vs-dev ~1% time gap from the per-trial logs (trial-1 first use of the frozen variant?). Pick the latest freeze whose population mean meets the acceptance rule (N_rule).

Progressive/stochastic freeze (Drop-Muon style). Over the last ~40% of samples, detach group 1 on each step with a probability rising linearly from 0 to 1. The expected frozen fraction equals the 85% hard freeze (~15% of samples), using the same two warmed graph variants selected per step on the host (group-1 params skip Muon/SGD on frozen steps; momentum untouched). Prediction: at equal total time (+/-0.5%), accuracy is >=0.04 pp better than the 85% hard freeze on >=100 trajectories each. Low prior: evidence comes only from tiny CNNs and training-accuracy metrics, and MosaicML found no Pareto gain.

Deeper late freeze: from ~92% of samples (floor-hold + final-EMA window), detach group 2's output too (no backward into stem, group 1 or group 2), warmed as a third static 32 px graph variant. Prediction: >=2% additional saving over the stem + group-1 freeze at the same point, with an extra loss <=0.06 pp on >=100 trajectories. If the extra loss is >=0.1 pp, the late-freeze depth is capped at group 1.

Free analysis: pool E113's arms A and B (200 E100 trajectories, mean ~0.7530, SE ~0.018) as the standing baseline, and keep appending new E100 trajectories. Recompute E114 and E116 against it. Prediction: E114 ~ +0.045 pp and E116 ~ -0.09 pp (SE ~0.032 each), i.e. E116 trades ~0.025 pp per 1%. From now on every large-seed arm is compared with this pooled baseline, not a single 100-seed vector.

Gate economics and acceptance rule. With per-trajectory sd 0.26 pp, a recipe with population mean mu passes the local 3-seed gate with p ~ Phi((mu-0.753)/0.15) and the official 40-seed 0.75 bar with p ~ Phi((mu-0.75)/0.041). Rule: bank a candidate if its >=200-trajectory (or >=100 vs the pooled baseline) population mean is >=0.7518 (official pass >99.99%) and it produces a scored row >=0.753 within <=3 scored attempts. All discretionary --force keeps and discards (E096, E100 kept; E110, E103 discarded) are re-judged by this rule, not by single scored draws.

Free check on existing logs: for every same-code family with >=3 distinct scored samples and a >=22-seed off-seed or large-seed mean (E046 family, E070 family, E090, E100), the scored pass fraction and the scored mean agree with Phi((mu-0.753)/0.15) and mu within binomial or 2-SE error. Example: E100 mu ~0.7530, predicted pass ~50%, observed 4/5. If any family's distinct scored mean exceeds its population mean by >2*0.15/sqrt(n), the one-component model is incomplete for the scored harness.

Before pairing E116's loss with an update-count gain: run E104 code (bs 1024 in all phases, +2.8% time) untimed on >=100 seeds vs the pooled E100 baseline. Prediction (H10): +0.08 to +0.15 pp (>=2.5 SE). If it lands at <=+0.04, the update-count rate is not real, and 'bs 1024 everywhere + 85% freeze' is not a net lever.

Re-measure the reference trim rate on the large-seed instrument: E100 with the 32 px phase cut by 0.25 epoch (samples-indexed, LR/EMA/tail rescaled, all shapes warmed), >=100 trajectories vs the pooled E100 baseline, plus the scored time. Prediction: a loss of 0.15-0.35 pp for ~-5% time (0.03-0.07 pp per 1%). The measured rate (+/-~0.01 pp per 1%) replaces the 0.065 yardstick that freeze, width and depth levers must beat.
